---
title: "Backends"
---

A **backend** is the AI provider an agent dispatches to. Autosprint supports
two — **Claude** and **Copilot** — and reaches each one in a genuinely
different way. This page explains how model access works, what you need
installed and authenticated for each, and how autosprint verifies access
before a long run.

The short version: **autosprint holds no API key and passes none.** It
delegates authentication entirely to the tool you have already logged into.

## The agent / backend model

An *agent* is a plain dict defined in the
[registry](architecture.qmd) (`registry/agents/`):

```python
{"assistant": "claude",  "model": "claude-opus-4-8", "system_prompt": "...", "tools": TOOLS_FULL}
{"assistant": "copilot", "model": "gpt-5.2",         "system_prompt": "...", "tools": TOOLS_FULL}
```

The `assistant` field is the only thing that selects a backend. Every LLM call
funnels through `infra/dispatch.py`, which looks `assistant` up in a
registry-of-functions and calls the matching dispatcher:

```python
DISPATCHERS = {"claude": _run_claude, "copilot": _run_copilot}
```

The phases above `infra` never import an SDK directly — they call
`query_agent()` / `query_agents()` with an agent dict and a prompt, and stay
backend-agnostic. Adding a third backend is one entry in that dict plus one
`_run_*` function.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-backends
%%| fig-cap: "The assistant field routes each agent to one of two dispatchers, which reach their models by different mechanisms."
flowchart TD
  phases["phases — call query_agent / query_agents"]
  dispatch["infra/dispatch.py<br>DISPATCHERS"]
  claude["_run_claude"]
  copilot["_run_copilot"]
  cli["claude CLI<br>(subprocess on PATH)"]
  api["GitHub Copilot API<br>(direct HTTP)"]
  phases --> dispatch
  dispatch -->|assistant = claude| claude
  dispatch -->|assistant = copilot| copilot
  claude -->|spawns| cli
  copilot -->|calls| api
```

## Claude — a local CLI agent harness

The `claude-agent-sdk` does **not** make HTTP calls to the Anthropic API
itself. It **spawns the `claude` CLI (Claude Code) as a subprocess** and drives
it through a streaming message protocol.

That means model access for Claude agents is *whatever your local `claude`
install is authenticated to*: your Claude Code login (a Pro/Max subscription
session) or an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` present in the CLI's own environment.
Autosprint neither knows nor cares which — it only requires the `claude` binary
on `PATH`.

- **Install:** [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).
- **Required on PATH:** `claude`.
- **Authentication:** handled by the CLI (`claude` login, or the CLI's env).

## Copilot — the SDK calls the API directly

The `github-copilot-sdk` is a pure Python package that **calls GitHub's Copilot
API directly** — no subprocess, no PATH binary. Model access here is your
**GitHub Copilot subscription**, whose session the SDK resolves on its own.

- **Install:** the `github-copilot-sdk` Python dependency (already in
  `pyproject.toml`).
- **Required on PATH:** nothing.
- **Authentication:** your existing GitHub Copilot session.

## Authentication summary

|                             | Claude                                                  | Copilot                                         |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Mechanism                   | `claude-agent-sdk` **spawns the `claude` CLI**          | `github-copilot-sdk` **calls the API directly** |
| Needs on PATH               | `claude` binary (hard-required)                         | nothing                                         |
| Auth source                 | local Claude Code login / its env's `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | GitHub Copilot subscription session             |
| Does autosprint hold a key? | No                                                      | No                                              |
| Token accounting            | counted (can be per-token)                              | not counted (flat-rate subscription)            |

The token-accounting asymmetry is encoded in the dispatcher: it tallies Claude
prompt/response characters for an end-of-run usage estimate but deliberately
skips Copilot, because a flat-rate subscription's call count does not reflect
cost.

## Verifying access before a run

Only the backends your configured team actually uses are probed —
`_required_assistants_for_run` collects the `assistant` kinds across `TEAM`,
`IMPLEMENT_AGENT`, the implement fallback, and `HOWFAR_AGENT`. A Claude-only
setup is never asked for Copilot auth, and vice versa.

Two layers of checking:

- **Static pre-flight** (`init` / startup): `claude` on `PATH` for Claude;
  importability of the Copilot SDK. Fast, but cannot tell you the login is
  still valid.
- **Live round-trip** (`autosprint doctor`): one cheap real call per backend in
  use, confirming auth and dispatch end to end. This catches an expired login,
  a hit usage cap, or a Copilot SDK that lost its bundled binary *before* a
  multi-hour run starts limping. The live probe is skipped in debug/cache modes
  (`LOG_LEVEL <= 15`) so dev loops and tests never make live calls.

```bash
autosprint doctor   # PATH check + one live round-trip per backend in use
```

If a backend is misconfigured, `doctor` prints the full checklist and the run
path refuses to start rather than failing confusingly mid-sprint.

## Choosing backends

Team composition lives in `registry/teams.py` and is selected with the `TEAM`
config var (see [Configuration](configuration.qmd)). Because the phases only
ever see strings and dicts, you can mix providers freely — e.g. Claude planners
with a Copilot selector, or a Claude implementor with a Copilot fallback.
Single-provider users have ready-made teams:

- **Claude only:** `TEAM=solo_opus`.
- **Copilot only:** `TEAM=solo_gpt55`.
